newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan steel output seen steady in April-June.
newsitem.headline: Japan steel output seen steady in April-June.

text.p: Japan's steel output in the April-June quarter is likely to hold steady near the January-March quarter's expected 25.5 million tonnes, Takashi Imai, chairman of the Japan Iron and Steel Federation, said on Friday.
Imai, who is also president of Nippon Steel Corp, said strong growth in demand and a drawdown in inventories would help output remain at its recent higher levels.
"Except for a few items for which there was overproduction, inventory adjustments are largely complete," he told reporters.
He added that the recent weakening of the yen to what he said were appropriate levels had also reduced the likelihood of any increase in import pressures on domestic producers.
The Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) is scheduled to announce its April-June forecast for Japanese crude steel demand next week.
